What it tells you: A new RACF ID was created. It shows the request details and, when one was made, the number of the completion ticket for the app team.
When it is sent: After the bot creates a RACF ID and the job shows ENDED. For a SailPoint ticket, only while "Completion notices for SailPoint tickets" is On.
Subject (Japanese / English): アカウント登録完了 / Provisioning completed — <ticket>
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
What must be switched on: Transaction outcome emails = On (Settings > E-mail; restart needed).
How to test it: Create a test RACF ID: Requests > New request (Application = Fujitsu RACF, Create), or raise a SailPoint new-account test ticket. Check the mailbox when the request shows Completed.

What it tells you: A RACF ID was removed, or was already removed. It shows the number of the completion ticket for the app team when one was made.
When it is sent: After the bot removes a RACF ID and the job shows ENDED. For a ServiceNow ticket (removal, transfer, termination or certification), only while "Fujitsu RACF removals" = Remove the whole RACF ID.
Subject (Japanese / English): アカウント削除完了 / Deprovisioning completed — <ticket>
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
What must be switched on: Transaction outcome emails = On (Settings > E-mail; restart needed). For tickets: Fujitsu RACF removals = Remove the whole RACF ID (Settings > Fujitsu RACF).
How to test it: Remove the test RACF ID: Requests > New request (Application = Fujitsu RACF, Remove), or raise a removal test ticket.
Latest change: A completion ticket is now also created for certification removals by default.

What it tells you: The request could not be completed. It gives the reason and what to do next.
When it is sent: Once, after the last attempt: the job ended with JCL ERROR, the job ABENDED every time, or the screen did not respond as expected.
Subject (Japanese / English): 【要対応】<ticket> の依頼を完了できませんでした / Action required: request for <ticket> could not be completed
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
Sent with the default settings?: No. The general error e-mail (No. 18) is sent instead.
What must be switched on: Transaction outcome emails = On (Settings > E-mail; restart needed).
How to test it: Preview it under Settings > E-mail > E-mail samples. A live test needs a command that fails, agreed with the Fujitsu RACF team.

What it tells you: The command was sent but its result could not be read. Check the RACF ID by hand and do not retry. The ticket stays open.
When it is sent: No SUBMITTED line or no job result after about three checks. The request shows Needs verification.
Subject (Japanese / English): 【要確認】<ticket> の処理結果を確認できませんでした / Please verify: the result for <ticket> could not be confirmed
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
Sent with the default settings?: No. The general error e-mail (No. 18) is sent instead.
What must be switched on: Transaction outcome emails = On (Settings > E-mail; restart needed).
How to test it: Preview only: a live test would need the host to stop answering right after the command.

E-mail: Request rejected – handled by a person (Fujitsu RACF)
What it tells you: A Fujitsu RACF removal ticket was left for a person, and why. The ticket is told the same.
When it is sent: A removal, transfer, termination or certification ticket arrives while "Fujitsu RACF removals" = Left for a person (the default).
Subject (Japanese / English): 依頼受付不可 / Request rejected (手動対応 / Handled by a person) — <ticket>
Who receives it: Operations
What must be switched on: Transaction outcome emails = On (Settings > E-mail; restart needed).
How to test it: Keep Fujitsu RACF removals = Left for a person, raise a removal test ticket, then System > Check ServiceNow now.

E-mail: Request rejected – ticket values not valid (Fujitsu RACF)
What it tells you: A Fujitsu RACF ticket could not be processed, with the reason in one sentence. Examples: the RACF ID is longer than 8 characters, the RACF group or Employee ID is missing, or the ticket adds more than one group. Also sent for a duplicate of an open request.
When it is sent: When the bot reads such a ticket from ServiceNow.
Subject (Japanese / English): 依頼受付不可 / Request rejected (入力不備 / Validation failed) — <ticket>
Who receives it: Operations
What must be switched on: Transaction outcome emails = On (Settings > E-mail; restart needed).
How to test it: Raise a test ticket with a 9-character RACF ID, then System > Check ServiceNow now. (A wrong value typed on the console form is refused on screen, with no e-mail.)

What it tells you: Fujitsu RACF refused the bot's password. Fujitsu RACF requests wait until it is fixed; Fujitsu Mainframe keeps running.
When it is sent: At sign-on, when the host shows PASSWORD NOT AUTHORIZED ... REENTER.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF サインオン拒否 / sign-on refused — password not accepted — <ticket>
Who receives it: The Fujitsu RACF team and operations. The CyberArk / identity team is added when CyberArk supplies the Fujitsu RACF password.
How to test it: Only with the Fujitsu RACF team's agreement (lock-out risk): pause processing, store a wrong Fujitsu RACF password under Settings > Credentials, run Test Fujitsu RACF sign-on, then put the correct password back at once.

What it tells you: The bot's Fujitsu RACF password has expired. Fujitsu RACF requests wait until it is set again.
When it is sent: At sign-on, when the host says the password has expired.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF サインオン拒否 / sign-on refused — password expired — <ticket>
Who receives it: The Fujitsu RACF team and operations. The CyberArk / identity team is added when CyberArk supplies the Fujitsu RACF password.
How to test it: Preview "Recognised error screen (owning team) — TSS_PASSWORD_EXPIRED" under E-mail samples.

What it tells you: The bot's Fujitsu RACF sign-on ID is revoked. Fujitsu RACF requests wait until it is restored.
When it is sent: At sign-on, when the host says the ID is revoked.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF サインオン拒否 / sign-on refused — sign-on ID revoked — <ticket>
Who receives it: The Fujitsu RACF team and operations.
How to test it: Preview "Recognised error screen (owning team) — TSS_ID_REVOKED".

E-mail: Sign-on refused – sign-on ID not authorized
What it tells you: The bot's sign-on ID may not use Fujitsu RACF. Fujitsu RACF requests wait until access is given.
When it is sent: At LOGON, when the host says USERID ... NOT AUTHORIZED TO USE. No password is typed.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF サインオン拒否 / sign-on refused — sign-on ID not authorized — <ticket>
Who receives it: The Fujitsu RACF team and operations.
How to test it: Preview "Recognised error screen (owning team) — TSS_ID_NOT_AUTHORIZED".

What it tells you: The sign-on was refused with a message the bot does not know. The request ends and is not retried.
When it is sent: At LOGON or after the password, with a message not listed in the Fujitsu RACF screen settings.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF サインオン拒否 / sign-on refused — message not recognised — <ticket>
Who receives it: The Fujitsu RACF team and operations.
How to test it: Preview "Recognised error screen (owning team) — TSS_LOGON_REJECTED_UNRECOGNISED".

What it tells you: The same e-mail as No. 7 to 11, sent for a test from the console. It names the person who ran the test.
When it is sent: Test Fujitsu RACF sign-on is run on the console and the host refuses the sign-on. (An ID in use sends No. 14 instead.)
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF サインオン拒否 / sign-on refused — <reason> — コンソールのサインオンテスト（富士通 RACF） / Console sign-on test (Fujitsu RACF)
Who receives it: The Fujitsu RACF team and operations. The CyberArk / identity team is added when CyberArk supplies the Fujitsu RACF password.
How to test it: Pause processing, then Settings > Fujitsu RACF terminal and sign-on > Test Fujitsu RACF sign-on during the Fujitsu RACF hours. The result says whether the e-mail was sent.

E-mail: Fujitsu RACF not available – host not answering
What it tells you: The Fujitsu RACF host does not answer. Fujitsu RACF requests wait in the queue; Fujitsu Mainframe keeps running.
When it is sent: The regular host check fails (every few minutes). Once per outage.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACFが利用できません / Fujitsu RACF Not Available
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
What must be switched on: Fujitsu RACF host and port set (Developer, This machine).
How to test it: Make the host unreachable from the bot server, then Settings > Fujitsu RACF > Test Fujitsu RACF host.

E-mail: Fujitsu RACF not available – sign-on ID in use
What it tells you: The bot's sign-on ID is still signed on somewhere else. No password was typed. Fujitsu RACF requests wait and the sign-on is tried again.
When it is sent: LOGON REJECTED ... IN USE, during a request or a sign-on test. Once.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACFが利用できません / Fujitsu RACF Not Available
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
How to test it: Sign on with the bot's ID in another window, then run Test Fujitsu RACF sign-on. Sign off the other window afterwards (No. 17 follows).

E-mail: Fujitsu RACF not available – host says not available
What it tells you: The host answered that it is not available. No password was typed. Fujitsu RACF requests wait.
When it is sent: At sign-on, during a request or a sign-on test. Once per outage. At present the general error e-mail (No. 18) is also sent while Transaction outcome emails is Off.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACFが利用できません / Fujitsu RACF Not Available
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
How to test it: Only possible while the Fujitsu RACF team has the host in maintenance.

E-mail: Fujitsu RACF not available – terminal could not start
What it tells you: The Fujitsu RACF terminal could not be started on the bot server. Fujitsu RACF requests wait; the start is tried again every few minutes.
When it is sent: The terminal did not start or did not show SYSTEM READY. Once per outage.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACFが利用できません / Fujitsu RACF Not Available
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
How to test it: Pause processing, rename the Fujitsu RACF shortcut named in the settings (for example add .off), run Test Fujitsu RACF terminal launch, then rename it back.

What it tells you: Fujitsu RACF works again. The waiting requests run.
When it is sent: The first good check after a "Not available" e-mail (No. 13 to 16). No outage e-mail means no recovery e-mail.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACFが復旧しました / Fujitsu RACF Recovered
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
How to test it: After No. 13, 14 or 16, remove the cause and run the same test again.

What it tells you: An error recorded by the Fujitsu RACF automation, in plain words.
When it is sent: An error without its own e-mail. With the default settings this is the e-mail for a failed job or an unconfirmed result. The same error is sent at most once every 5 minutes.
Subject (Japanese / English): 【エラー】富士通 RACF の自動処理でエラーが発生しました / Error: an error was recorded in Fujitsu RACF automation
Who receives it: Operations and the Fujitsu RACF team
How to test it: With Transaction outcome emails Off, run a request that fails.

What it tells you: A summary of the alerts and failed requests since the last summary, Fujitsu RACF included.
When it is sent: Daily at 09:00 JST (or hourly), only when there was at least one alert. Also when the service stops.
Subject (Japanese / English): 日次サマリー（<date>）：処理失敗 n 件、その他 n 件 / Daily summary for <date>: n failed requests, n other issues
Who receives it: Operations only.
How to test it: Produce a Fujitsu RACF alert (No. 18), then System > Restart service.

What it tells you: The report of one Fujitsu RACF SailPoint ticket: RACF ID, RACF group and result.
When it is sent: Once per Fujitsu RACF SailPoint ticket, when its request has finished, whatever the result.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF アカウント<action>報告 / Fujitsu RACF Account <action> Report (<date>)
Who receives it: The support report recipients (blank = operations) and the Fujitsu RACF team.
What must be switched on: Transaction outcome emails = On (Settings > E-mail; restart needed). Support report per SailPoint ticket = On (default).
How to test it: Raise a Fujitsu RACF new-account test ticket and wait until the request is finished.

E-mail: Registration notice to the new user (Fujitsu RACF)
What it tells you: Tells the new user their RACF ID and RACF group, and the rule for the initial password. Never contains a password. Japanese first, then English.
When it is sent: After each RACF ID created from a SailPoint new-account ticket, while its switch is On. Not sent without a valid address for the user.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF アカウントの新規登録について（通知）/ [Notice] New Registration of Fujitsu RACF Account
Who receives it: The new user (from the ticket), with the Registration notice CC copied when it is set (for example the app team).
Sent with the default settings?: No (Off until the client agrees the wording)
What must be switched on: Transaction outcome emails = On (Settings > E-mail; restart needed). Registration notice to the new user (Fujitsu RACF) = On (restart). Optional: Registration notice CC (Fujitsu RACF).
How to test it: Keep "Send every e-mail only to (testing)" set to your address, switch the notice On, then raise a new-account test ticket.

What it tells you: The Fujitsu RACF password could not be fetched from CyberArk. The bot does not sign on until CyberArk delivers it.
When it is sent: Only where CyberArk supplies the Fujitsu RACF password: a fetch failed at start, at a refresh or on Refresh CyberArk now. Once per outage.
Subject (Japanese / English): CyberArk が利用できません（ボットのパスワードを取得できませんでした） / CyberArk not available: the bot could not retrieve its password
Who receives it: The CyberArk / identity team and operations.
What must be switched on: CyberArk in use for the Fujitsu RACF password.
How to test it: Make CyberArk unreachable from the bot server, then System > Refresh CyberArk now.

What it tells you: CyberArk delivers the password again.
When it is sent: The first good fetch after No. 22.
Subject (Japanese / English): CyberArk が復旧しました / CyberArk Recovered
Who receives it: The CyberArk / identity team and operations.
How to test it: After No. 22, remove the block and select System > Refresh CyberArk now.

What it tells you: The service started but Fujitsu RACF cannot run, with the reason. For example the Fujitsu RACF password is not stored. Fujitsu Mainframe is not affected.
When it is sent: At each start of the service while Fujitsu RACF is on and one of its parts did not start.
Subject (Japanese / English): サービス起動（問題あり）/ Service started with problems
Who receives it: Operations only.
How to test it: On a test server: remove the Fujitsu RACF password under Credentials, then System > Restart service. Put it back afterwards.

What it tells you: The bot's Fujitsu RACF password has reached the age at which it should be changed (80 days by default). The bot cannot change it itself: ask the RACF administrators, then enter the new password under Credentials and the new date in "RACF sign-on ID password: last changed on".
When it is sent: Checked every hour; sent once a day until the password is changed. Only when the date of the last change is known.
Subject (Japanese / English): 富士通 RACF サービスアカウントのパスワード変更時期です / Fujitsu RACF service-account password change due
Who receives it: Operations, the CyberArk / identity team and the support report recipients.
Sent with the default settings?: Only after "RACF sign-on ID password: last changed on" is entered.
What must be switched on: RACF sign-on ID password: last changed on = the real date (Settings > Fujitsu RACF terminal and sign-on).
How to test it: On a test server: enter a date 82 days ago in "last changed on", save, then wait for the hourly check (or Check password age now). Put the real date back afterwards.

What it tells you: Urgent: the bot's Fujitsu RACF password expires within a few days (5 by default). After the expiry no Fujitsu RACF request can be processed.
When it is sent: From 5 days before the expiry (90 days by default), once a day until the password is changed.
Subject (Japanese / English): 【至急】富士通 RACF サービスアカウントのパスワードの有効期限が近づいています / URGENT: Fujitsu RACF service-account password expires soon
Who receives it: Operations, the CyberArk / identity team and the support report recipients.
Sent with the default settings?: Only after "RACF sign-on ID password: last changed on" is entered.
How to test it: As No. 25, with a date 87 days ago.

What it tells you: Urgent: the bot's Fujitsu RACF password may have expired, so the bot can no longer sign on. Ask the RACF administrators to reset it, then enter the new password and the new date on the console.
When it is sent: On and after the expiry date, once a day until the password and date are updated.
Subject (Japanese / English): 【至急】富士通 RACF サービスアカウントのパスワードの有効期限が切れています / URGENT: Fujitsu RACF service-account password has expired
Who receives it: Operations, the CyberArk / identity team and the support report recipients.
Sent with the default settings?: Only after "RACF sign-on ID password: last changed on" is entered.
How to test it: As No. 25, with a date 91 days ago.
